<!-- pr-reviewer: e7d53147011bf2cbf3a3344d12f2b9d9f5344fdf -->
**Needs changes before merge** - one gap in the law text. Everything else is ready.

Reviewed against #1320 and the scope change in its comment (collaborators count). The head was trial-merged with `origin/main` at 4ea96bd5 without conflicts.

### What looks good
- **Rule reversal (A).**
  - The three new quotes match the decision exactly:
    - "Any collaborator review counts";
    - "Both collaborators";
    - "everyone counts. everyone needs to get merged, mkinney and i are coolaboration across the world on the same code base".
  - The PROCESS_VERSION 31 rule is kept as history: "Superseded since 2026-11-12, later the same day", with its quote "No, only ours count".
  - All quoted maintainer sentences on main are still present word for word in the PR's AGENTS.md. The only string that changed is the section title "Only the owner's reviews count", which was a cross-reference, not a quote.
  - The collaborator rule appears in AGENTS.md, `review-prs`, `resolve-conflicts`, `PR-reviewer.md` and the new skill. Each place points back to AGENTS.md "Only collaborators' reviews count".
  - No sentence about reviews, markers or merge labels still says owner-only.
  - Cuts and tags stay with the maintainer. A non-collaborator's PR still waits for the user.
- **The new step-1 query works live, read-only.** `COLLABS` = `NeoTech mkinney dudedagger42`.
  - #972, whose only head marker is by mkinney, is no longer listed.
  - #1310, whose only head marker is by `seelesturm` (not a collaborator), is listed.
  - #1112 and #961, with markers from both collaborators, are not listed.
- **Skill (B).** `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md` runs end to end with only `gh`, `git` and `cargo xtask merge-plan`. It has no home-directory path and no Python. All the asked-for safety rules are there:
  - the user decides, nothing unapproved merges, and never `--approve`;
  - merge commits only, and fork branches are not deleted;
  - stacked children are retargeted before the parent merges;
  - wave 1, then wave 2 one PR at a time, and only the PR next in the batch is refreshed;
  - the `--delta` classes, the after-merge sweeps and one gate per batch;
  - no merge during a release cut. The precondition search `head:release/` does find `release/*` PRs; I checked.
- **Determinism (C).**
  - `HashMap`/`HashSet` are gone from all merge_plan files. The simulated-commit cache is a `BTreeMap`.
  - Every choice goes through a named key ending in the PR number, and conflicted-file lists come from git, which sorts them.
  - Live, `cargo xtask merge-plan 1319 1314 1311 1310 1309` gave byte-identical output on two runs and with the numbers reversed. The plan was wave 1 #1309, #1319, #1314; wave 2 #1310 by hand, #1311 mechanical.
  - `--json` parses. The full base sha and each head sha are printed, and the scratch refs were deleted after each run.
  - The tests are meaningful: shuffled input gives the same plan, there is one test per tie-break, and JSON escaping is covered.
- **Hygiene.**
  - `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is 32, against main's 31.
  - The #681 text says plainly that it reverses version 31 and what a fork must do.
  - There is no workflow trigger and no new dependency.
  - `Changelog: none`, and the single commit is `build(process)`.
  - Files are at most 391 lines, with no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests.

### Local results (merged with main 4ea96bd5)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p xtask` | 88 passed, 0 failed (11 in `merge_plan_det_tests`) |
| `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo xtask merge-plan` x2, then reversed order | identical |
| `cargo xtask merge-plan --json` | valid JSON |

### Requested before merge
1. **Two collaborator reviews of the same head that disagree.** No text covers this case. With two collaborators reviewing, the same head can carry one review ending "Ready" (`merge-ready`) and another listing requested changes. Then the label is simply whichever review ran last, and `/merge-ready` step 1 keeps the PR whenever `merge-ready` is set and a collaborator marker exists for its head. Please add one rule to AGENTS.md "Only collaborators' reviews count", repeated in `review-prs` step 2b and `merge-ready` step 1. For example: "If collaborator reviews of the current head disagree (one clean, one with requested changes), the requests stand: the label is `needs-rework`, `/merge-ready` reports the PR and does not merge it until the requests are addressed in a new push or withdrawn by the reviewer who made them."

### Notes (not blocking)
- **Collaborators list for non-collaborators.** GitHub serves `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators` only to accounts with push access. The skill's "anyone else may run steps 0-2 read-only" will get a 403 at step 1 for a fork's non-collaborator agents. Say so, or let them skip the `COLLABS` line and plan their own PRs only.
- **Pagination.** `gh api .../collaborators` without `--paginate` reads the first 30 accounts only. That is fine today with three; `--paginate` makes it future-proof.
- **MECHANICAL wording (carried over from #1227).** AGENTS.md "Every PR opens as a draft" sends a MECHANICAL refresh back to draft for review "as usual", while the skill's wave 2 says "`SAME` or `MECHANICAL` -> merge it now". One clause ("for MECHANICAL, the merging session's own read is the review") would align them.
- **Gate count.** The skill's after-merge gate fires "when two or more code PRs merged". AGENTS.md runs a gate after a single fix merge too, so say "one or more".
- **Process-file list.** The skill's after-merge list and the #681 announcement leave out `.cargo/config.toml` and the `scripts/gate.*` / `release.ps1` / `collect-decisions.*` wrappers. AGENTS.md's process-file sync list has them all.
- **"The main session merges them".** AGENTS.md "fix / perf / refactor PRs ... the main session merges them" could now read "a collaborator's session merges them", to match the new rule.
- **Claim rules still say "the owner account"** ("agents post as the owner", the 4 h rule). That is outside #1320's scope, but with mkinney's agents posting as mkinney it is worth a follow-up issue.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 8fd1a98e2a1ea4597b3f3ad32cda6be7b9f8c020 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

This is a read-only re-check of the one commit added since my last review, 8fd1a98e "build(process): a requested change stays open until addressed", on top of e7d53147. I read the diff and did not build: the commit changes text only, and my review of e7d53147 already built and tested the code (88 xtask tests passed, clippy clean).

### The requested change is addressed
- The disagreement rule is stated once, in AGENTS.md "Only collaborators' reviews count".
  - A request for changes on a head stays open until it is addressed: either a new head that a collaborator's review clears, or the requesting reviewer withdrawing it in a comment.
  - Another collaborator's `merge-ready` label or "ready" review on the same head does not override it.
  - A head that carries both is a disagreement: `/merge-ready` reports it and does not offer it, no agent removes either label, and the two collaborators settle it on the PR.
- The other three texts only point to that rule, and they agree with it and with each other:
  - `merge-ready` step 1: report the PR, leave it out, change neither label.
  - `review-prs` step 2b: no agent removes either label.
  - `PR-reviewer.md` step 7: leave both labels and say so in the report.
- Keeping both labels unchanged, rather than my suggested `needs-rework`, is sound. The PR still cannot merge, because `/merge-ready` leaves it out. It also stops two reviewer loops from flipping the label back and forth.
- The commit touches only those 4 files (+21/-1). The one removed line is the `PR-reviewer.md` label sentence, rewritten with the exception. No quoted maintainer sentence is touched.
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is still 32 against main's 31.
- The head still merges cleanly with `origin/main` 4ea96bd5 (git merge-tree), and GitHub reports `MERGEABLE`.

### Notes (not blocking)
- **How a requesting review is recognised.** Our review requests are review comments, not GitHub "changes requested" reviews. `/merge-ready` step 1 could say how it spots one: the verdict line under a collaborator's `pr-reviewer` marker for the head ("Needs changes before merge"), with no later withdrawal by that reviewer.
- **After a clean merge of main.** If the head moves by a merge of main that `--delta` classes SAME, the open request should still count. "Current head" could read "the current head, or an earlier head that `--delta` classes SAME or MECHANICAL", the same reach the merge-ready cleanup already uses.
- **`review-prs` wording.** Its first clause, "A requested change that is still open on the current head ... is a disagreement", is a little wider than AGENTS.md, which needs both the request and `merge-ready`. It is harmless, because the effect is only "no agent removes either label".
- The earlier non-blocking notes from my review of e7d53147 still apply.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
